# brainfreeze studio

brainfreeze studio turns a RAPP agent (a person's Brainstem, a RAPP Store rapplication, or a frozen rapp/1 egg)
into a Copilot Studio agent in their own environment. An agent with a translation that brainfreeze studio ships
becomes agent flows or connector code, proven against the agent's real Python; the Brainstem's own memory agents
become Copilot Studio memory tools when their code is the reviewed original; every other agent becomes a skill, and
the build says why. The deploy runs with the person's own sign-in.

Primary user instruction:
Put my agent in Copilot Studio.

Public entry point:
https://kody-w.github.io/rapp-brainfreeze-studio/

Setup skill (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and any AI agent that can run commands):
https://kody-w.github.io/rapp-brainfreeze-studio/skills/brainfreeze-studio/SKILL.md

Machine-readable setup contract:
https://kody-w.github.io/rapp-brainfreeze-studio/brainfreeze-studio.json

Source and documentation:
https://github.com/kody-w/rapp-brainfreeze-studio

Rules:
- The person signs in themselves (az login) and picks the environment from their own list.
- Say what you will install, and wait for their yes.
- The build runs the agents' Python on this computer to prove translations; it isn't a sandbox, so build only
  code the person trusts.
- Build once. Plan that build with --plan (read-only), show what it would create, update or remove, and wait for
  yes. Then deploy exactly that build with the plan's --expect <digest>.
- Deploy as a Draft (--draft). Publish only when the person asks.
- Quote the build's parity lines; never claim a translation the build refused.
- Report a reply from Copilot Studio only if you saw it in the person's signed-in browser; otherwise give them
  the link and the question, and say you haven't seen the reply.
- Never use a service account, an app-only token or someone else's connection; never change anything in the
  environment beyond what the plan lists.
- Never print or store a token.
